title: Traffic-driven SLO adjustment with regional failover and circuit-breaker guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our existing SLO work captures static per-endpoint targets but does not adapt to sudden traffic shifts across regions or reallocate error budget between model variants during partial degradation. We observed two incidents where region-specific saturation caused disproportionate retries and poor global tail latency despite global error budget headroom. Goal: Design a traffic-driven SLO adjustment and orchestration policy that: 1) defines compact, measurable SLIs per model variant and route; 2) dynamically rebalances error budget to prioritize critical paths when traffic shifts; 3) enforces region-aware circuit breaker hysteresis to avoid cascading failovers; and 4) provides deterministic load-shedding rules that preserve high-value requests. This ticket defines the policy, required metrics, rollout plan, monitoring, and runbook artifacts for engineering and on-call teams.
acceptance_criteria: SLO/SLI spec document approved by Reliability and Product owners describing primary and secondary SLIs for text-generation, chat-stream, and embeddings routes.
Algorithm for traffic-weighted error-budget reallocation documented with pseudo-code and unit tests in runtime repo.
Circuit breaker and failover thresholds defined per region and per model tier; accompanied by simulation results showing reduced cascading failures in 3 fault scenarios.
Load-shedding policy implemented as config-only rules (no code changes required for first rollout) with canary enabled and default safe-mode behavior.
Dashboards and alerting configured: SLI leaderboards, per-region error budget consumption, CB tripping events, and synthetic probes; alerts created with on-call runbook links.
Playbook entries for on-call describing steps for manual override, forced reallocation rollback, and post-incident analysis template.
End-to-end integration test demonstrating controlled failover from us-east to europe-west with preserved P95 latency degradation within SLO budget in canary environment.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design): finalize SLI names, measurement windows, and reallocation algorithm. Educate stakeholders.
Phase 1 (sim): run 10 synthetic traffic scenarios in staging (regional spike, model degradation, network partition) and tune thresholds.
Phase 2 (canary): enable policy for low-traffic customer segments and a single region for 72 hours with enhanced logging.
Phase 3 (gradual): roll out by traffic-weight bands (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with automated rollback on policy alarm.
Phase 4 (GA): enable globally, publish runbook and SLO dashboard, and schedule 30-day postmortem review for tuning.
metrics_and_sli: Primary SLI (availability): successful-response-rate measured as 1 - (errors / total_requests) over 1m and 30m windows per route/model_variant/region.
Primary SLI (latency): P95 generation latency measured end-to-end (request ingress -> final token emitted) with tag dimensions: route, model_variant, region.
Secondary SLI (quality): small sampling of completed responses passed through existing eval prompts; weekly regression percent.
Operational SLI: CPU/GPU backpressure signals and request queue length per serving pool used as a leading indicator for load-shedding decisions.
Measurement notes: use unified metrics prefix rwi.sli.<route>.<model>.<region> with 1m/5m/30m rollups; ensure cardinality controls for large model catalogs.
circuit_breaker_policy: CB levels: WARNING (soft), TRIP (hard), COOLDOWN. Each level defined per model_variant-region pair.
Soft warning: if 1m error-rate > 1% AND 1m P95 latency > 2x baseline -> emit warning event, slow start new connections for 30s.
Hard trip: if 5m error-rate > 3% OR queue depth > 4x steady-state for 5m -> open circuit for region-model_variant for 2 minutes then probe.
Hysteresis: require both downward trend for two consecutive windows (5m and 15m) before closing CB to avoid oscillation.
Fallback behavior: on hard trip, traffic routed according to failover map (region-preference -> secondary region -> degraded model variant) with rate-limited surge protection.
Observability: CB state transitions emit events to tracing and dashboard; include sample payloads for debugging.
error_budget_reallocation: Every 5 minutes compute per-route error-budget-usage (EBU) across regions and model_variants for last 30m.
When a region is consuming >70% of its regional error budget AND global budget has >20% spare capacity, temporarily borrow up to min(15% of global spare, region need) for up to 30 minutes.
Borrowed budget assigned as 'boost' with TTL; each boost creates immutable audit event and must be visible on SLO dashboard.
Priority ordering: critical routes (auth, billing, low-latency customer-facing) receive reallocated budget before non-critical. Priority mapping stored in config with admin override.
Automatic rollback: if reallocated region sees error-rate increase >50% in next 10 minutes, revoke boost and mark incident for postmortem.
load_shedding_policy: Graceful shedding strategy: prefer dropping/queuing lower-priority routes and non-interactive batch embeddings before throttling chat or auth-critical paths.
Decision signals: GPU queue pressure, request queue length, active inference sessions, and cache hit ratios influence shedding threshold.
Tiered shedding: 1) degrade to cheaper quantized variant, 2) reject non-critical requests with 429 + Retry-After, 3) shed based on token-budget-per-request caps for long-running generations.
Client signal: include structured error payloads with reason codes to enable client-side degrade patterns (e.g., stream partial, shorten max_tokens).
Audit: all shed events logged with request sample id, model_variant, region, and SLO state for post-incident analysis.
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: SLI leaderboard, region heatmap of error budget, CB state timeline, top shedding reasons, and per-model latency distribution.
Alerts: P0 alert when global error budget consumption > 90% and more than one region is > 70% consumption; P1 alert for CB hard trip events affecting >5% of traffic.
Synthetic probes: per-region synthetic requests for representative routes every 30s; failures count against SLI but flagged as synthetic in analytics.
Logging: sample request traces (1:10k) including model variant selection, routing decision, CB decision path, and any reallocation action.
testing_plan: Unit tests for reallocation algorithm covering borrowing, TTL expiry, and rollback conditions.
Simulation harness: replay historical traffic with injected region failure and verify policy produces expected routing and budget changes.
Chaos test: scheduled partition in staging with varying degrees of latency and error amplification to test hysteresis and shedding thresholds.
Canary test: A/B test 1% traffic with policy enabled vs control for 72 hours; compare SLOs and business metrics.
